name: aribb24
desc: Library for ARIB STD-B24, decoding JIS 8 bit characters and parsing MPEG-TS
why: Decodes ARIB Japanese broadcast captions from MPEG-TS, a door into obscure broadcast standards.

brief.what_it_is: A library for ARIB STD-B24, the Japanese broadcast standard for captions and text. According to the Homebrew description, it decodes JIS 8-bit characters and parses MPEG-TS streams, so it takes an MPEG transport stream carrying ARIB caption data and produces decoded caption text. The scout note describes it as decoding ARIB Japanese broadcast captions from MPEG-TS. I could not read the README to confirm the details, so treat this as the formula's description rather than the author's own.
brief.why_it_exists: The README did not load, so I could not confirm the author's framing. The formula description only says it is a library for the ARIB STD-B24 standard.
brief.install_notes: Nothing verified beyond the Homebrew formula. It lists no executables, so it is presumably a library for other software to link against rather than a command-line tool. I did not see build steps, dependencies, or configuration.
brief.standout: It is a door into obscure broadcast standards: ARIB STD-B24 is the Japanese digital broadcast caption format, which most English-language developers never encounter. The project is hosted on the VideoLAN GitLab, which suggests a link to the VLC/libav ecosystem, though I did not confirm that from the README.
brief.status: unknown. The GitLab project page shows it was created on October 14, 2019. I saw no release, last-commit date, or maintenance note because the README and project activity did not load.
brief.caveats: I could not read the README, so this brief rests on the Homebrew description and scout notes. The homepage was reachable only as a GitLab shell; the README and raw file were blocked by an Anubis proof-of-work challenge that requires JavaScript. No license terms were confirmed, though the project has a LICENSE file. No commands, API examples, or platform notes were verified.
